figure: Root cause: officials' account, no written report
source_and_why: On the record, Duffy says legacy analog TDM switches and routers were overloaded with data and gave inconsistent data, so the FAA shut the system down; Mullin says new equipment and patches overwhelmed the old system. No written FAA root-cause report, vendor or specific upgrade has been named, and the FAA newsroom still says "communication issues." [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/3fec1b0a85a0/world/us/faa-issues-national-ground-stop-due-extraordinary-circumstance-reasons-safety-2026-11-13/) · [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/the-faa-nationwide-ground-stop-is-over/) · [FAA statement](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-statement-nationwide-ground-stop) · Still Reported, not confirmed: CBS (an update to the private ATC network caused a reboot), Bloomberg (one unnamed person: the FBI is looking at a software update), and CNN via Fox 5 Vegas (began with routers, possibly at Midway). FAA Advisory 005, signed 8:19 PM ET with event time 8:16 PM ET, says the FAA Command Center nationwide ground stop has been cancelled, destination ALL, facilities ALL, with no reason given and the next update at 11 PM ET. IFR Meter timed the cancel at 8:16 PM, 4 hours 22 minutes after the stop was ordered. The stop ended nationwide at once, not by a published center-by-center release. [Advisory 005](https://www.fly.faa.gov/ois/oisedit/adv_oisedit_dis?day=11142026&number=005) · [IFR Meter](https://ifrmeter.com/blog/national-ground-stop-2026-11-13)

ABC quotes Duffy's Saturday morning post announcing a 10:30 AM ET press briefing at DOT headquarters with FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford, and saying operations are slowly returning to normal and "it is safe to fly."
